Microneedling can be a great tool for hair growth, but only if it’s done correctly.

A few things I recommend before adding microneedling into your hair-loss routine:

✨ Skip the dermaroller! I prefer a dermastamp for more controlled, vertical penetration with less pulling on the hair.
✨ Keep your device clean and replace the needles regularly.
✨ Consistency matters more than being overly aggressive.

✨ Get scalp inflammation, dandruff or seborrheic dermatitis under control first.

Both create tiny microchannels in the skin to stimulate collagen—but they work very differently.

✨ Microneedling Pen
Pros:
✔️ Adjustable needle depth for different areas of the face
✔️ Covers large areas quickly
✔️ More consistent needle penetration
✔️ Great for professional treatments and advanced skin concerns

Cons:
✖️ More expensive
✖️ Requires a specific technique
✖️ Higher risk of irritation if used incorrectly

✨ Derma Stamp
Pros:
✔️ Easier for beginners to control
✔️ Better for treating small, targeted areas
✔️ More affordable

Cons:
✖️ Takes longer to treat the entire face
✖️ Fixed treatment area means more stamping
✖️ Shorter lifespan—the same needles are used repeatedly and can gradually become dull over time, which may make treatments less effective and potentially more uncomfortable.
